technique: 3D CGI rendered to imitate stop-motion/claymation: felted-fiber cloth shaders on the woman's sweater and the man's suit (visible fuzzy fiber texture, most obvious in periodic-5 through periodic-10 close-ups), smooth painted-clay skin on the elongated wedge-shaped noses and necks, and glass-marble eyes with a fixed static specular dot that doesn't relight as the head turns (periodic-8 to periodic-11). Unlike genuine stop-motion, motion between adjacent periodic frames (periodic-0 to periodic-3, the walk cycle) is continuous and sub-pixel-smooth with no frame-doubling, no armature jitter, and no fingerprint/tool marks on the surfaces — this is a digital puppet rig built to read as tabletop stop-motion rather than the genuine article. Confidence: high on 'CGI made to look like stop-motion'; the exact rig (blendshape face vs. joint-based) can't be confirmed from stills alone.
facial_animation_notes: Faces are minimal and mask-like: a static painted mouth-line that only changes shape (open oval for 'wrong'/'argument' in periodic-6 and periodic-9, closed smile in scene-1) with no visible teeth, tongue, or cheek deformation around it. Eyebrows do the heavy lifting for expression — compare the man's flat brows in periodic-9 vs. the sharply raised, spread brows in periodic-10/11/12 during the closeup 'take' — this is a clean shape-swap rather than a gradual muscle-driven change, consistent with morph-target/blendshape animation rather than sculpted-clay replacement (no seam lines or texture discontinuities appear when the brow shape changes).
eye_and_blink_notes: No blinks are caught in any of the periodic frames despite several being seconds apart, and the round glass-bead eyes keep an identical fixed white sclera and black pupil dot in nearly every frame, only changing via eyelid-shape (heavy lower lid droop in periodic-5/6/9 vs. wide-open circular in periodic-10/11/12). The specular highlight on each eye stays glued to the same relative position across head turns (e.g., periodic-6 vs. periodic-9), a giveaway that it's a shader highlight rather than a physically relit reflective surface.
head_movement_notes: Head turns are slow and continuous, e.g., the man's head rotates smoothly toward camera between periodic-8 and periodic-11 with intermediate angles well-covered rather than snapping between poses. There's a small independent tilt/tuck of the chin during the reaction close-up (periodic-9 to periodic-11) that reads as an eased ease-in/ease-out curve, not a linear or stepped rotation.
gesture_notes: Arms stay largely locked at the sides holding the plastic grocery bags through the walk and elevator sequence (scene-0 through periodic-7); no free hand gesture is caught in any sampled frame, suggesting gesture is sparse/withheld in favor of facial and postural reaction (the pulled-back torso and raised brows in the close-up carry the comedic beat instead of hand acting).
idle_motion_notes: Between dialogue-bearing frames the poses are close to held rather than continuously fidgeting — the couple's stance in scene-0/periodic-2/periodic-3 barely differs in arm or leg position aside from the walk-cycle leg swap, giving a slightly 'posed' quality between beats rather than constant secondary idle sway.
frame_rate_feel: Source is 30fps per metadata.json, and motion sampled across the periodic frames (which are seconds apart) shows fully continuous interpolation — no stepped/held-frame stutter, no doubled poses, and smooth in-between head/eye states are implied by the fluid progression of expressions. This reads as animated at or near full frame rate rather than on 2s/3s stop-motion holds, despite the deliberately clay-like surface look.
overall_animation_style_notes: The film pairs a deadpan, limited-gesture performance style (stiff walk, bag-holding arms, minimal mouth shapes) with painterly stop-motion-coded surfacing (felted cloth, matte clay skin, glued-on glass eyes) to evoke an Aardman-style dry British sitcom look while actually being produced with smooth CGI rigging — the comedic timing lives almost entirely in eyebrow/eyelid shape changes and slow head reveals (periodic-8 through periodic-12) rather than broad body movement.
